topic: Sanctions, shadow-fleet exports, and Train 3 status (2025-2026)
wiki_text: Arctic LNG 2 (Novatek-led, Gydan Peninsula) continues to operate under US/EU sanctions that have severely constrained offtake. Train 2 began production around May 2025 even as Train 1 was unable to sell cargoes for lack of sanctions-compliant tankers; by June 2025 an LNG vessel call at the plant pointed to a possible export restart via Russia's assembled 'shadow fleet', whose capacity remains far below what full three-train output would require. TotalEnergies' exit from its 10% stake was cleared by Russian authorities in 2025. Train 3 construction had largely stalled in 2024 — Novatek postponed the third line to 2028 (from 2025) — but in late April 2026 the first known Train 3 pipe-rack modules departed China for Russia, the first sign of renewed Train 3 module movement. Russia's Energy Strategy to 2050 (April 2025) lists the full project for commissioning by 2030.

topic: Unresolved ExxonMobil stake after Sakhalin-1 withdrawal
wiki_text: Far East LNG at De Kastri is tied to the Sakhalin-1 consortium. ExxonMobil (via Exxon Neftegas, ~30%) announced its withdrawal from Sakhalin-1 in 2022 and took multi-billion-dollar writedowns; by Russian presidential decree the project was transferred to a new Russian-domiciled operator (Sakhalin-1 LLC). Exxon's ~30% interest has not been reassigned to a confirmed successor, leaving roughly 30% of the Far East LNG ownership 'unknown' in trackers, alongside SODECO (~30%), ONGC (~20%) and Rosneft affiliates (Sakhalinmorneftegaz-Shelf 11.5%, RN-Astra 8.5%). Reporting through 2025-2026 indicates the De Kastri liquefaction trains are unlikely to come online before 2035. GEM retains the 'unknown [30%]' slice pending a verified transfer.
